subject: AWS Marketplace metering & entitlement — timeline, checklist and contract questions
messages:
From: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme-analytics.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AWS Marketplace metering / fulfillment questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the product overview last week — ACME is excited about Redwood as a potential marketplace offering. Two procurement items came up after our review and I wanted to get clarity before we schedule the legal kickoff: 

1) Metering dimensions — our billing team needs to confirm the exact usage dimension (monthly active users vs. vCPU-hours vs. inference-unit tokens). Can you confirm what Redwood expects to publish to AWS as the metering dimension and whether you support dual-dimension reporting?

2) Fulfillment & entitlements — we need to know how entitlements are mapped to our org: will AWS issue entitlements per Marketplace subscription and then Redwood map to our account ID? Any constraints on contract start/renewal dates?

3) Contract redlines — our legal team prefers a SaaS contract as the primary customer agreement with a marketplace fulfillment addendum. Do you provide a seller-side fulfillment addendum template we can review?

If possible, please send a short checklist (technical + procurement) and an estimated timeline for go-live (assuming no major redlines). I can loop in our procurement lead (CCed) if that helps.

Best,
Jill Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering / fulfillment questions

Hi Jill — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a proposed next step below. Looping in Sean (sales lead) and Marissa (partner ops) who own fulfillment.

- Metering dimension: our default for Marketplace SaaS is a single "meteringDimension" per listing. For inference-heavy use cases we commonly publish a token-based metering (tokens/inference-hour). We can also support a seat-based MAU dimension for enterprise accounts but that requires mapping entitlements to directory IDs. Dual-dimension reporting is not standard in AWS Marketplace metering — it increases complexity on the billing side — but we can discuss options.

- Entitlements: AWS issues entitlements per subscription SKU. Redwood consumes the entitlement via the AWS Marketplace entitlement API and maps it to the customer using the customer_id you provide (tenant ID). Renewals are bound to the Marketplace subscription lifecycle; start/renew dates typically match the subscription effective date but we can align contract terms on the seller offer.

- Contract redlines: we have a fulfillment addendum template and a SaaS contract stub. Marissa, can you attach the checklist + the fulfillment addendum draft and suggest typical timeline?

Proposed next step: 30-min technical/ops sync this week to validate metering dimension and entitlement mapping (I can host). What times work for you?

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme-analytics.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering / fulfillment questions

Hi Jill — quick commercial context from my side:

• Pricing model: we can support either a per-token metering SKU (recommended for inference-heavy workloads) or a seat/MAU SKU for enterprise usage. Per-token gives you more granular billing but is slightly more work on your end to validate usage dimensions.
• Billing and invoices: AWS will invoice ACME for the Marketplace subscription and remit to Redwood according to the Marketplace settlement schedule. If you require Redwood to invoice directly (invoice-before-settlement), we can discuss a private offer / seller-furnished billing flow but that adds steps to procurement.

Marissa — can you confirm the typical lead time from our side for the seller offer to be published once entitlements + contract are agreed? Also please attach the fulfillment addendum that Jonas requested.

Jill — happy to join the sync. My availability Thu/Fri 10:00-13:00 PT.

Best,
Sean
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme-analytics.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering / fulfillment questions

Thanks all — attaching the checklist and a draft fulfillment addendum. High-level steps and estimated timeline below (assuming no major legal redlines):

1) Confirm metering dimension (1-3 business days)
   - We need the exact dimension name you want published (e.g., redwood:inference_tokens, redwood:maus). If token-based, provide expected monthly volume ranges for quota planning.

2) Technical integration (3-7 business days)
   - Redwood will enable the entitlement consumer pipeline in our account and validate the entitlement API calls against a test subscription.
   - We will provide a short script to validate entitlement consumption on your side.

3) Contract & procurement (5-15 business days)
   - We attach: SAAS_FULFILLMENT_DRAFT_2026-02.pdf (fulfillment addendum) and procurement_terms_redlines.docx (typical redlines we accept). Please return with your redlines in DocuSign if possible.

4) Seller offer publication (2-4 business days after paperwork)
   - Once the seller offer is live, AWS will start issuing entitlements; we will complete mapping and kick off any migration steps.

Action items: 
- Jill/Acme: confirm metering dimension and expected volumes (reply to this thread).
- Jonas/Sean: propose a 30-min slot (Jonas suggested hosting).
- ACME legal: please review and upload redlines to DocuSign link (https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF-ACME-2026).

Notes / risk items:
- Dual-dimension billing is possible but will typically require a custom seller offer and explicit AWS approval — expect extra 2-3 weeks.
- If ACME requires Redwood to invoice directly outside the marketplace, that moves to a private offer and lengthens procurement.

Attachments included: redwood_aws_metering_checklist.xlsx, SAAS_FULFILLMENT_DRAFT_2026-02.pdf, procurement_terms_redlines.docx

Let me know if you want me to start the DocuSign envelope and I’ll pre-fill common fields.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Partner Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
